headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-chaining between Dify and pdf.js can leak data and cascade errors; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present via file content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge base files and use tools wired into agent/workflow apps, while pdf.js processes PDF files in a browser-based worker. If Dify passes PDF-derived text into prompts, malicious PDF content could steer downstream instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Dify ingests pdf.js-extracted text into an agent prompt without provenance tagging
IF a PDF contains instruction-like text that is forwarded from pdf.js to Dify
mitigations: Tag PDF-derived text as untrusted before prompt assembly
Strip instruction-like sections from extracted PDFs
Add a human review step for PDFs that will be summarized
Separate raw PDF text from system/developer prompt channels
requires-engineering: enforce provenance-aware prompt templating

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and model-provider/tool credentials, and its concurrency model shares state via the Dify server datastore. pdf.js touches PDF documents and files. If both run against the same workspace or datastore, sensitive document content can flow into Dify logs or outputs even though pdf.js itself has no network egress.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem or shared datastore
IF PDF contents are copied into Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base uploads
mitigations: Store PDFs in a separate directory from Dify logs
Disable retention of conversation logs for sensitive runs
Restrict Dify uploads to redacted PDFs only
Review shared datastore permissions
requires-engineering: isolate workspaces per agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem, execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; pdf.js can run browsers and read PDF files. Their write/read overlap is enough for conflicts if they share a directory or orchestrator state, even though pdf.js lacks write or network capabilities. The shared-state risk is real but not as severe as unrestricted dual-write.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Dify writes artifacts that pdf.js reads during the same run
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Make pdf.js inputs read-only
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Avoid letting Dify write into the PDF source tree
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or orchestrator-level mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can produce agent/workflow outputs and act through tools, while pdf.js is a document-processing worker. If pdf.js output is treated as authoritative by Dify, extraction errors or malformed PDF text can cascade into downstream actions or summaries. Because Dify has action-capable tooling and pdf.js is not a verifier, the default risk is more than low.
conditions: IF Dify uses pdf.js output as a source of truth without verification
IF Dify triggers tools or workflows based on extracted PDF text
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on extracted text
Show source snippets alongside summaries
Limit automated actions from PDF-derived outputs
Flag low-confidence OCR or extraction results
requires-engineering: add cross-checking against the original PDF

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content, while pdf.js touches PDF documents. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is evident: retention and logging policies may differ if the same PDF data is processed by both. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from their combined handling of the same documents.
conditions: IF the same PDF contains regulated personal data and is retained in Dify logs
IF retention settings differ between Dify conversation logs and pdf.js processing artifacts
mitigations: Minimize logged content in Dify
Delete temporary PDF artifacts after processing
Use redacted PDFs for shared workflows
Document retention periods for both systems
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
